set_title: Nail signs: Clubbing, Koilonychia, Beau lines, Mees lines, Nail pitting and Terry nails
stem: A 44-year-old farmer has had 3 weeks of abdominal pain, vomiting, a garlic odor on his breath and a painful stocking-glove neuropathy. Transverse white bands cross his fingernails (Mees lines). He recently used an old pesticide stored in his barn.
oneliner: 44M farmer, abdominal pain + neuropathy + white transverse nail bands → poison?
ask: Which poison best explains this sign?

whyNot.A: Lead gives wrist drop and basophilic stippling; he has **garlic breath**
whyNot.B: Mercury causes tremor and gingivitis; he has **garlic breath and Mees lines**
whyNot.C: Carbon monoxide gives headache and cherry-red skin; he has **stocking-glove neuropathy**
whyNot.E: Cyanide gives bitter almond breath and rapid collapse; his course is **weeks of neuropathy**

why: Transverse white nail bands are Mees lines, a marker of arsenic poisoning. **Abdominal pain, garlic breath and neuropathy** complete the picture; treat with dimercaprol or succimer.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Loss of nail fold angle, bulbous tips
Nail growth arrest: chemotherapy, severe illness
Small punched-out pits in nail plate
White nail with thin distal red band

idea.rule: Transverse white nail bands + neuropathy + garlic breath = Mees lines = arsenic.
also: Raises skin and lung cancer risk

set_title: Odor clues: Fruity breath, Fetor hepaticus, Bitter almond odor, Garlic odor, Musty (mousy) body odor and Maple syrup urine
stem: A 52-year-old man with hypertensive emergency has received a high-dose nitroprusside infusion for 3 days. He becomes confused and tachypneic, with arterial pH 7.18 and lactate 11 mmol/L. His breath smells of bitter almonds.
oneliner: 52M, 3 days of nitroprusside + confusion + lactic acidosis + bitter almond breath → ?
ask: Which toxin best explains this presentation?

whyNot.A: Organophosphates cause miosis, secretions and bradycardia, not **lactic acidosis on nitroprusside**
whyNot.C: Carbon monoxide follows combustion exposure; he is on a **nitroprusside infusion**
whyNot.D: Methanol follows ingestion with visual disturbance, not a **nitroprusside infusion**
whyNot.E: Arsenic smells of garlic with GI toxicity and neuropathy, not **bitter almonds**

why: Nitroprusside releases cyanide, which blocks cytochrome oxidase (complex IV) and halts aerobic metabolism, causing **lactic acidosis** and bitter almond breath.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Musty smell of urine and sweat

idea.rule: Nitroprusside + lactic acidosis + bitter almond breath = cyanide toxicity.

set_title: Mouth and gum clues: Oral hairy leukoplakia, Oral thrush, Burton lines, Gingival hyperplasia and Atrophic glossitis
stem: A 38-year-old man who recycles car batteries has 3 weeks of colicky abdominal pain, constipation and weak wrist extension. Hemoglobin is 9.2 g/dL with basophilic stippling. A thin blue-gray band runs along the gum margin of his lower incisors.
oneliner: 38M, battery recycler + colicky pain + wrist weakness + blue-gray gum margin band → ?

whyNot.A: Hairy leukoplakia is on the lateral tongue; his finding is at the **gum margin**
whyNot.B: Thrush is white and wipes off; his band is **blue-gray at the gum margin**
whyNot.C: Gingival hyperplasia is gum overgrowth; his gums have a **blue-gray band**
whyNot.E: Atrophic glossitis involves the tongue; his abnormality is at the **gum margin**

why: A blue-gray band along the gum margin is a Burton line, lead sulfide in the gingiva; **basophilic stippling and wrist weakness** confirm lead poisoning.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Ridged white lateral tongue plaques, not scrapable

idea.rule: Blue-gray gingival band + abdominal pain + stippling = lead poisoning (Burton line).
also: Lead inhibits ALA dehydratase and ferrochelatase

set_title: Mouth and gum clues: Oral hairy leukoplakia, Oral thrush, Burton lines, Gingival hyperplasia and Atrophic glossitis
stem: A 24-year-old man with epilepsy for 3 years has gums that have overgrown his teeth and bleed with brushing. He also has coarse facial features and excess body hair. His seizures are well controlled.
oneliner: 24M, epilepsy + overgrown bleeding gums + coarse facies + hirsutism → ?
ask: Which drug most likely caused this finding?

whyNot.A: Carbamazepine causes hyponatremia and agranulocytosis, not **gum overgrowth with hirsutism**
whyNot.B: Valproate causes hepatotoxicity, tremor and alopecia, not **gum overgrowth with hirsutism**
whyNot.C: Lamotrigine causes rash, not **gum overgrowth and coarse features**
whyNot.E: Ethosuximide treats absence seizures with GI upset, not **gum overgrowth**

why: Overgrown gums with **coarse facies and hirsutism** in an epileptic patient indicate phenytoin; cyclosporine and calcium channel blockers also cause gingival hyperplasia.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Ridged white lateral tongue plaques, not scrapable

idea.rule: Gum overgrowth + hirsutism on an antiseizure drug = phenytoin.
also: Cyclosporine and nifedipine also cause it
Phenytoin: cerebellar signs, teratogenic, megaloblastic anemia
